subject.title: Feature: temp artifact provenance + durable-path guardrails to prevent /tmp chaos

question: Should OpenClaw core own a general temp-artifact provenance and cleanup model, or only the runtime-critical temp-path guardrails plus a minimal plugin/skill seam?
rationale: The issue is valid but the durable storage owner, cleanup authority, and boundary between core safety checks and workflow-specific janitor behavior require maintainer intent before implementation.

options.title: Core guardrails plus minimal provenance seam
options.body: Have core cover runtime-critical temp-path checks and a SQLite-backed provenance contract for OpenClaw-owned artifacts, while workflow-specific classifications live in plugins or ClawHub packages.

options.title: Full core provenance registry
options.body: Build a core-owned artifact classification and cleanup policy for all first-class OpenClaw temp artifacts, accepting broader state and janitor responsibility in core.

options.title: Plugin or skill-only workflow
options.body: Keep artifact provenance outside core except for concrete bug reports and publish the janitor/classification workflow through ClawHub.

recommendation.title: Core guardrails plus minimal provenance seam
recommendation.body: Have core cover runtime-critical temp-path checks and a SQLite-backed provenance contract for OpenClaw-owned artifacts, while workflow-specific classifications live in plugins or ClawHub packages.

likelyOwner.reason: This account has the strongest combined history in temp-root hardening, guardrail scripting, and core-vs-plugin scope decisions for this area.
